Question: I want to treat rice seeds with Azospirillum and Phosphobacteria, how much water should I mix with 5 packets of each for soaking overnight?
AgentAnswer: Hey, if you have five packets of Azospirillum and five packets of Phosphobacteria, you can start by putting them in a container and adding about 15 litres of water. That’s roughly between ten and twenty litres, which is a good middle ground. Mix well until the powders are fully dissolved. Then add your rice seeds and let them soak overnight. If you have a lot of seeds, you might need a little more water so everything stays wet, but keep it close to that range. Remember, this is just a starting point – it can change a bit depending on how many seeds you have and how strong you want the solution to be. If you’re unsure, it’s best to ask someone at your local agriculture office for a quick check. Good luck with your rice!

Question: Sir, my paddy field soil is very fluffy. What can I do to prevent my animals and workers from sinking during puddling?
AgentAnswer:
If your paddy soil feels like a soft pillow and you see people sinking when you try to puddle, first make the ground a little firm. Take a heavy stone roller that weighs about 400 kilograms or use an oil‑drum filled with stones. Roll over the field about eight times while the soil is moist – the right moisture is when the soil feels a little damp, not dry, but not soaking wet. Do this once every three years. 

Next, when you puddle, use a machine that can make a smooth, tight layer under the water. You can use a cage wheel, a rotavator, or a power tiller with a rotary tool. These machines help form a layer that keeps the water from running away and makes the soil less soft. 

If your soil is salty, you can spread some gypsum – use about half of the amount that the soil needs – and let water collect for a while so the salt can move out. After that, put some green leaf manure on the field about ten to fifteen days before you plant. 

Always start puddling when the field has about four to six inches of water. Keep that water level steady while you work. 

So, firm up the soil with the stone roller, use a proper puddling machine, keep the right amount of water, and if the soil is salty, add gypsum and green manure. That will help your animals and workers stay on their feet while you work the paddy.

Question: Sir, I am cultivating Ponni rice variety, its growth period is 150-155 days, can I grow it in submerged conditions?

For Ponni, it is safest to keep the water level about 10 to 15 centimeters, not more than 20 centimeters. If the water stays very deep for a long time, the rice may not grow well. I am not 100 percent sure about how deep Ponni can tolerate, so it is best to keep it shallow and ask your local agriculture office for more advice.

Question: Sir, my rice nursery is ready but canal water has been delayed. What should I do?
AgentAnswer: Sir, if the canal water is late, keep the nursery wet by any means you can. You can use a small amount of water from a bucket or a small container. Aim to keep the soil moist enough that you can feel a few centimetres of water on the surface. That means about the depth of a small cup of water held over the bed. Keep it for two or three days before you transplant. If you have a drip system or a small irrigation pipe, you can run it slowly to keep the soil saturated. Cover the beds with a light cloth or use a few layers of straw or cloth to keep the soil from drying. If you have any leftover water, pour it in. If you do not have any water, try to use rainwater if it comes. Keep the seedlings damp and wait until the water comes. When the canal opens, finish filling the beds and transplant the seedlings. If you are unsure, ask the local agriculture office for help.

Question: Sir, I want to use biofertilizer for my paddy seeds. Should I use 1 kg or 125 ml of Azospirillum for 1 hectare of seeds?

Question: Sir, my Improved White Ponni rice crop is getting blast disease, what protection measures should I take?
AgentAnswer: Hello. If your Improved White Ponni rice is showing blast, do these things. First, plant varieties that are already known to resist blast. Second, keep a good rotation of crops; don’t plant rice in the same place every year. Third, use only clean seeds that you know are free from disease. Fourth, look at your fields often. If you see a little spot, spray a fungicide when the plants are at the late boot stage – that is when the flower is just starting to form. Then spray again when most of the plants have started to head, about when 80 to 90 percent are in that stage. You can also use a natural fungicide called Trichoderma, which is safe and helps fight the blast. Keep the leaves clean and dry; avoid overwatering. Use a mix of these steps, not just one. If you are unsure about how much of a spray to use, ask a local officer or a farmer who has used it before. That will give you the right amount. Good luck with your crop.

Question: Sir, I am cultivating TKM 11 rice variety, its duration is given as 110-120 days, but my crop is maturing in 100 days, what is the problem?
AgentAnswer: Hello, I see you are growing TKM 11 rice and it is maturing earlier than expected. This can happen for a few reasons. First, make sure the seed you are using is really the TKM 11 variety. Sometimes farmers get mixed seeds and the crop behaves differently. Second, the weather in your area may be warmer or cooler than usual. Warmer temperatures can make the plant finish its life cycle faster. Third, the soil and the way you are farming it can affect the growth time. If the soil is very fertile or you are giving it more water or nutrients than usual, the plants may grow quicker. To fix it, check the seed lot, try to plant the seedlings a bit later if the weather is hot, and keep the soil and water management normal. Also remember that for short‑duration varieties like this, you normally transplant seedlings that are about 18 to 22 days old. If you are transplanting them too early or too late, that can also change the time to maturity. If you are unsure, you can ask your local agriculture office for help. They can check the variety and give you specific advice for your farm. Good luck with your rice.

Question: Sir, I want to sow rice seeds immediately. If I treat with Pseudomonas fluorescens and soak overnight, how to make seeds ready for sowing?
AgentAnswer: Good morning. To treat your rice seeds with the bacteria and sow them right away, follow these simple steps. First, get the bacteria solution – it is a liquid that contains the Pseudomonas bacteria. For each kilogram of rice seeds you have, pour about five millilitres of that liquid into a clean bowl. Add the seeds to the bowl and stir them gently so that every seed gets a light coat of the liquid. Leave the seeds in this mixture for about 18 hours. Keep the bowl in a warm place, but do not let it dry out completely. After 18 hours, take the seeds out and spread them on a clean cloth. Let them dry a little – just until they are not sticky. Now the seeds are ready to be sown in your fields. If you are unsure about the amount of liquid or the exact time, you can ask the local agriculture office for help. They can give you the right guidance for your specific area. Good luck with your planting.

Question: Sir, my paddy crop in Nagapattinam district is flooded during NE monsoon, how to manage waterlogged soil for better yield?
AgentAnswer: Sir, if your paddy fields are flooded during the monsoon, here is what you can do. First, try to get the water out. Make small drainage channels or open existing ones so the excess water can flow away. After the water level goes down, make the soil airy. You can dig small holes or use a hoe to break the surface so the roots can breathe. Next, give the plants a good dose of nutrients. A mix of urea, DAP and potash will help the rice grow again. You can spray a little zinc on the leaves to fix any zinc shortage. Keep an eye on any pests or diseases and treat them early. Finally, give the crop a quick foliar boost – a light spray of nutrients on the leaves will help them recover faster. If you need exact amounts of fertilizer or zinc, ask the local agriculture office; they will give you the right numbers for your land. This way you can reduce the loss and get a healthy crop.

Question: Sir, my soil is clay, 20 cents land, how to make raised beds for paddy?
AgentAnswer:
Sir, to make raised beds on your 20 cents clay land, first find a flat part of the field. Use a stick or a piece of wood to draw a rectangle about five metres long and two metres wide. This will be one bed. If you want more beds, repeat the same size and leave a small gap between them for water to flow. 

Now dig a shallow trench around the rectangle, about thirty centimetres deep. Fill that trench with good soil and some compost if you have it. Then fill the inside of the rectangle with the same mix. Press the soil down gently so it is firm. Do the same for each bed you want. 

The raised beds will keep the clay soil from staying too wet. After the beds are ready, you can sow your rice seeds. Water the beds evenly but do not let them sit in water for long. That is how you make raised beds for paddy on clay soil. If you are unsure, ask the local agriculture office for help.
